# Review
## Correctness
**PASS.** The proof uses the published distinct-powers characterization to reduce attainable digit sums to nonnegative count triples in the three residue classes generated by \(b^3\equiv1\pmod{b^2+b+1}\). The witnesses for \(3\), \(b+2\), and \(2b+1\) are explicit. Their semigroup covers every integer at least \(2b-1\). For the missing boundary \(2b-2\), subtracting the minimum coordinate preserves the congruence, cyclic relabeling leaves two residue classes, and the resulting positive multiple of \(n\) is forced to equal \(n\). The inequalities then force the reduced length to be \(b+2\), which contradicts the residue of \(2b-2\) modulo \(3\) unless \(b\equiv1\pmod3\), excluded by hypothesis. The packaged verifier independently checks the residue criterion and explicit witnesses for all admissible \(2\le b\le100\).

## Originality
**PASS.** The focal paper explicitly asks for Frobenius numbers of \(\operatorname{Out}(s_b,n)\) in the coprime setting. Exact searches for the formula \(2b-2\), the modulus \(b^2+b+1\), the digit-sum arc set, and the source question returned no theorem covering this family. Clokie et al. provide the strongest broader tool found: their distinct-powers criterion and reachability propagation theorem imply neither the three-generator sharp coverage nor the boundary obstruction. A previously checked general conductor bound for digit sums of multiples is also strictly weaker than this exact equality.

## Value
**PASS.** The result gives a closed, sharp Frobenius number on the first nontrivial cyclotomic order family and directly answers an infinite natural subfamily of a published Frobenius-number question. The family is structurally motivated by \(b^3\equiv1\pmod{\Phi_3(b)}\), not selected by a numerical cutoff, and the proof exposes why order three produces both explicit generators and a sharp obstruction.

The main residual originality risk is unindexed literature on exact digit-sum Frobenius numbers; no decisive competing statement was found in the searched primary literature or result index.

Self-review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.
